assignments.title: Week 18: Flight Club
assignments.html:
Optima
Academy Online
Mission: Move!
5th Grade PE · Unit 1.9 · Kicking & Striking
Week 18
🚀 Flight Club Challenge

Final week of the seasonal modules. Cool-down focus — these three help your body recover after weeks of training.

1
Toe Touch Stretch (Waterfall Stretch)

How to Do It:

  • Stand up tall with feet together.
  • Slowly bend forward and reach for your toes, keeping legs straight.
  • Let your arms "flow down" like a waterfall.
  • Hold for 10 seconds, then slowly stand up.

Benefits: Stretches hamstrings (back of the thighs) and lower back.

2
Forearm Plank

How to Do It:

  • Get into a plank position with arms straight and back flat.
  • Hold for 30 seconds without dropping your belly.
  • Challenge: Try tapping one shoulder at a time while holding the plank.

Modification: Try a knee plank if needed.

Benefits: Builds core and upper body strength.

3
Shoulder Rolls

How to Do It:

  • Stand or sit up straight.
  • Slowly roll your shoulders forward in a circular motion 5 times.
  • Then roll your shoulders backward 5 times.

Benefits: Loosens up the shoulders and neck.

🏃Activity Cue

Submit a video demonstrating the challenges. The more you do, the more points you get in Flight Club!

✅Flight Crew Check-In

Flight Crew, check in!

  • Compare this to your Week 2 Flight Club. How has your range of motion changed? What evidence do you have?
  • Which of the 5 fitness components did this challenge train most? Why?

Unit 1.10

Reflect on a real moment when you worked with others. Specific examples beat general statements every time.

1
Step 1

2
Step 2
Write One Paragraph (5–7 Sentences)

assignments.title: Flight Club Leadership Challenge
assignments.html:
Optima
Academy Online
Mission: Move!
5th Grade PE · Unit 1.10 · Teamwork & Cooperation
Unit 1.10
🚀 Flight Club Leadership Challenge

A teamwork test in the form of a movement game. Mirror Moves asks you to lead AND follow — both are leadership skills.

1
Set-Up
  • Students work in pairs
  • Partners stand about 3–5 feet apart
  • One student starts as the Leader
  • The other partner is the Mirror
2
How to Play
  1. The Leader begins making slow, smooth movements.
  2. The Mirror copies the movements as closely as possible.
  3. Movements should be controlled and safe.
  4. After 30–60 seconds, switch roles so both students get a turn.
3
Movement Ideas for Leaders

Leaders may choose from the following:

  • Arm circles (small or big)
  • Marching in place
  • Side steps
  • Gentle squats
  • Reaching up high or down low
  • Balancing on one foot
  • Slow turns or twists

Remind leaders to move slowly so their partner can follow.

🏃Activity Cue

What to submit: A short video or written reflection answering the questions below.

✅Flight Crew Check-In

Flight Crew, check in!

  • Was it harder to lead or follow? Why? Use specific evidence from your turn in each role.
  • What did you do to help your partner succeed? Did it work? How do you know?

assignments.title: Flight Club Card Challenge
assignments.html:
Optima
Academy Online
Mission: Move!
5th Grade PE · Unit 1.11 · Sportsmanship & Respect
Unit 1.11
🚀 Flight Club Card Challenge

Random exercises drawn from a deck of cards. Sportsmanship in action — you don't choose what comes up, and you finish what you draw. Bonus: stretches first.

1
Warm Up — Reach for the Sky

How to Do It:

  • Stand up tall with feet shoulder-width apart.
  • Stretch both arms up as high as possible, reaching for the sky.
  • Hold for 10 seconds, then relax.
  • Optional: Wiggle your fingers like you're grabbing stars!

Benefits: Stretches arms, shoulders, and back.

2
Warm Up — Hug Yourself

How to Do It:

  • Wrap your arms around yourself like you're giving a big hug.
  • Gently pull your shoulders forward while keeping your back straight.
  • Hold for 10 seconds, then switch arm positions (whichever arm was on top, switch it).

Benefits: Stretches shoulders and upper back.

3
Materials Needed
  • Option 1: A real deck of playing cards
  • Option 2: Internet access and the Calculator Soup Random Card Generator
4
Draw a Card
  • If using a real deck, shuffle and draw one card at a time.
  • If using Calculator Soup, select 1 card, click Draw, and see your result.
5
Match the Card to the Exercise

Use the chart below to know which exercise to do. The number or face value tells you how many repetitions.

Suit Exercise Example
♥ HeartsJumping Jacks8♥ = 8 jumping jacks
♠ SpadesPush-UpsK♠ = 13 push-ups
♦ DiamondsSit-Ups/Crunches4♦ = 4 sit-ups
♣ ClubsSquatsJ♣ = 11 squats

Card Values

  • Ace = 14
  • King = 13
  • Queen = 12
  • Jack = 11
  • Numbers = Same as card value
6
Complete 10–20 Draws

Each time you draw a card, complete the exercise before drawing another.

Challenge Options:

  • Beginner: Draw 10 cards.
  • Intermediate: Draw 15 cards.
  • Advanced: Draw 20 cards.
🏃Activity Cue

Reflection: Write 3–4 sentences answering:

  • Did stretching before the deck card challenge help you perform better and/or do more?
  • What other stretches do you think would be beneficial for this activity?
✅Flight Crew Check-In

Flight Crew, check in!

  • This challenge mixes strength (push-ups, squats) and cardio (jumping jacks). Which suit pushed you the hardest? Why?
  • How is drawing random cards similar to a real sportsmanship moment? What does it teach about handling what you can't control?

5th Grade PE · Unit 1.12 · Fitness Components
Unit 1.12

Design a fitness station that targets one of the five components. Real athletic trainers do this constantly — building stations that focus on one skill at a time.

1
Think First
Before You Design

Consider:

  • What does your chosen fitness component help your body do?
  • What movements match that component?
  • How will you make the station safe AND fun?
2
Your Task
Choose ONE Fitness Component
  • ❤️ Cardiorespiratory Endurance
  • 💪 Muscular Strength
  • 🔁 Muscular Endurance
  • 🤸 Flexibility
  • ⚖️ Body Composition (Healthy Choices & Balance)
3
Plan Your Station
Fill These In
  1. Station Name — give it a fun, descriptive name (e.g., "Heart Hero Hop Zone")
  2. Fitness Component — which one is the focus?
  3. Activity Description — what will students DO at your station?
  4. Equipment — list anything you need (or "no equipment")
  5. Safety Rule — one rule to keep everyone safe
  6. Time — how long should students stay (e.g., 30 seconds, 1 minute)?
✅Check for Understanding

Reflection paragraph:

  • Which fitness zone idea was your favorite?
  • Which would make your heart beat fastest?
  • Which helps you stretch your body?
  • Why is it important to train ALL five components, not just your favorite?
📝Weekly Reflection

If a player ONLY visited your station for a month, what fitness changes would they see? What changes would they NOT see? Why?

Make a poster that breaks down ONE fitness component — clear enough that a 4th grader could learn it just from your visual.

Choose a Fitness Component

assignments.title: Plank & Balance Challenge
assignments.html:
Optima
Academy Online
Mission: Move!
5th Grade PE · Unit 1.12 · Fitness Components
Unit 1.12
🚀 Plank & Balance Flight Club

After exploring all 5 fitness components, train two at once: muscular strength + balance. The plank is the ultimate test of core endurance, and the variations layer on body control.

1
Your Goal

We're going to build strong muscles and endurance in your arms, core, and legs — all while having fun and learning to balance your body.

2
How to Play
  1. Get into a plank position: hands on the floor under your shoulders, body straight from your head to your toes, and tighten your tummy.
  2. Hold the plank for as long as you can while keeping good form.
    • Don't let your hips drop or lift too high.
    • Keep breathing!
  3. Stop when it gets too hard to keep your body straight.
  4. Try again later and see if you can hold it longer than before.
3
Try These Variations
  • Side Plank: Lie on your side and lift your body on one arm and the side of your foot. Switch sides after a few seconds.
  • Leg Lift Plank: Lift one leg while holding a plank. Switch legs every few seconds.
  • Partner Plank: Face a friend and try to hold your planks at the same time. Cheer each other on!
4
What You're Practicing
  • Muscles & Strength: Strong arms, shoulders, and core muscles
  • Endurance: Muscles that can work longer without getting tired
  • Balance & Control: Staying steady and moving safely

Tips:

  • Focus on quality over time — it's better to hold a good plank than a long, sloppy one.
  • Cheer your friends if you're in pairs or a group.
  • Beginners can try a knee plank or a forearm plank instead of the full plank.
✅Flight Crew Check-In

Flight Crew, check in!

  • This challenge trains TWO fitness components at once. Which two? How do you know?
  • Which version was hardest for you? Why — was it strength, endurance, or balance that gave out first?

Optima
Academy Online
Mission: Move!
5th Grade PE · Unit 1.13 · Personal Space & Movement Safety
Unit 1.13

Design VR signs that help others move safely. Real PE teachers and gyms put safety signs everywhere — your design could actually work.

1
Step 1
Create a Sign or Symbol

In VR, design a sign, poster, or symbol that shows:

  • Personal space (like "Keep Your Distance" or "Bubble of Safety")

Use colors, shapes, or pictures to make it easy to understand at a glance.

2

Think about how players will actually see and use your sign. Place it where it matters — entrance, near a high-traffic area, or floating in the VR space as a reminder.

3
Step 3
Practice Safe Movement

Move around in VR while respecting personal space. Step back if you get too close to other objects or signs.

4
Step 4
Reflect

Write or record your answers:

  • What does your sign teach about personal space or movement safety?
  • How does it help people stay safe?
  • What did you notice about moving safely in VR?
  • Upload a picture of your sign/display.
📝Weekly Reflection

Where would your sign work best — and where would it be ignored? Why? Use what you know about spatial awareness to explain.

2

assignments.title: Jumping Jack Countdown
assignments.html:
Optima
Academy Online
Mission: Move!
5th Grade PE · Unit 1.13 · Personal Space & Movement Safety
Unit 1.13
🚀 Jumping Jack Flight Club Countdown

Cardio challenge with safety focus. Personal space matters here — make sure you have enough room to swing your arms and legs.

1
Your Goal

Get your heart and lungs working while having fun! Jumping jacks help improve cardiorespiratory endurance, which is your body's ability to keep moving without getting tired.

2
How to Play
  1. Stand with your feet together and your arms at your sides.
  2. Jump your feet out and raise your arms above your head at the same time.
  3. Jump back to your starting position. This is one jumping jack.
  4. Do as many jumping jacks as you can in 30–60 seconds while keeping good form.
    • Keep your core tight
    • Land softly on your feet
    • Breathe steadily
3
Variations & Challenges
  • Countdown Challenge: Start at 50 (or another number) and count down as you complete each jumping jack.
  • High Jumping Jacks: Jump a little higher or add a clap above your head for extra fun.
  • Slow & Steady: Go slower and focus on form and control.
  • Partner Challenge: Do jumping jacks side by side and cheer each other on.
4
Fitness Focus + Safety

Fitness Focus:

  • Cardiorespiratory Endurance: Strengthens your heart and lungs
  • Coordination: Helps your arms and legs move together
  • Energy & Stamina: Makes it easier to keep moving in games and activities

Tips:

  • Make sure there is enough space around you — personal space is important!
  • Keep your movements controlled and safe.
  • Take breaks if you get tired and try again.
🏃Activity Cue

Reflection Questions:

  • How many jumping jacks could you do in 30–60 seconds?
  • Did your heart beat faster or slower during the challenge?
  • How did keeping a steady pace help you do more?
  • Which variation did you like best and why?
✅Flight Crew Check-In

Flight Crew, check in!

  • How much personal space did you need to do this safely? Why is the bubble bigger for jumping jacks than for, say, push-ups?
  • Was this aerobic or anaerobic exercise? Use your breathing as evidence to decide.

assignments.title: Flight Club Wall Sit Countdown
assignments.html:
Optima
Academy Online
Mission: Move!
5th Grade PE · Unit 1.14 · Rhythmic Movement & Dance
Unit 1.14
🚀 Wall Sit Flight Club Countdown

Lower-body endurance test. Stand against a wall, slide down, and hold. It looks easy until the burn starts.

1
How to Play
  1. Find a clear wall space.
  2. Lean your back against the wall and slide down until your thighs are parallel to the floor, as if sitting in an invisible chair. Keep your knees directly above your ankles and your back flat against the wall.
  3. Hold this "chair" position for as long as you can, focusing on keeping good form.
2
Countdown Variation
  • Start by holding the position while counting down from a certain number (e.g., 30, 20, or 10 seconds).
  • Challenge yourself to reach zero without letting your thighs rise above parallel.
3
Difficulty Enhancements
  • Add a ball: Hold a small ball between your knees to engage inner thigh muscles.
  • Raise your hands: Extend your arms straight out in front of you or overhead to engage shoulders and core.
  • Single-leg lift: Carefully lift one foot off the ground for a few seconds, then switch legs to increase difficulty and balance challenge.
4
Safety Tips & Focus

Fitness Focus:

  • Muscular endurance: Keeps your thigh muscles working over time.
  • Strength: Strengthens quadriceps, hamstrings, glutes, and core.
  • Balance & focus: Helps improve stability and concentration while holding the position.

Safety Tips:

  • Avoid letting your knees go past your toes.
  • Keep your back flat against the wall.
  • Stop if you feel pain (muscle burn is okay, sharp pain is not).

Personal Challenge: Record how long you can hold the wall sit each day and try to improve your time. Think about which variations felt easiest or hardest and why.

✅Flight Crew Check-In

Flight Crew, check in!

  • Which muscle group did this challenge target the most — quads, hamstrings, or glutes? How do you know?
  • This is muscular endurance training, not strength. Why? Use what you've learned about reps, resistance, and time.

5th Grade PE · Unit 1.15 · Balance & Coordination
Unit 1.15
🚀 Wall Ball Toss Flight Club Challenge

Balance + coordination + reaction time, all in one. The wall is your teammate. Don't break anything.

1
What You Need
  • A small, soft ball (foam ball, tennis ball, or rolled-up socks)
  • A clear wall space with nothing breakable nearby
2
How to Play
  1. Stand a few steps away from a wall.
  2. Toss the ball gently against the wall using both hands.
  3. Watch the ball carefully and catch it after it bounces back.
  4. Repeat for a set number of catches or for 30–60 seconds.

Focus on using soft hands when catching and keeping your eyes on the ball at all times.

3
Variations (Choose One or More)
  • One-Hand Catch: Toss with two hands and catch with only one hand. Switch hands after 10 catches.
  • Speed Toss: Toss and catch the ball faster while staying in control.
  • Squat & Catch: Perform one squat after each catch before tossing the ball again.
  • Clap & Catch: Toss the ball, clap once, then catch it.
  • Balance Toss: Stand on one foot while tossing and catching the ball. Switch feet halfway through.
4
Safety + Fitness Focus

Safety Tips:

  • Use a soft ball and throw gently (we're not trying to put a hole in the wall!).
  • Make sure the area around you is clear.
  • If the ball goes too far, slow down and regain control before continuing.

Fitness Focus:

  • Coordination: Helps hands and eyes work together.
  • Reaction Time: Improves quick responses to moving objects.
  • Upper Body Strength: Builds arm and shoulder muscles through repeated tossing and catching.

Challenge Option: See how many clean catches you can complete in 30 seconds. Try to beat your own score next time!

✅Flight Crew Check-In

Flight Crew, check in!

  • The Balance Toss variation tests two skills at once. Which two — and which one limited your reps first? How do you know?
  • How did your hand-eye coordination change over the challenge? Did you get smoother — what evidence do you have?

assignments.title: My Fitness Goal & Plan
assignments.html:
Optima
Academy Online
Mission: Move!
5th Grade PE · Unit 1.16 · Goal Setting & Personal Fitness Plans
Unit 1.16

Time to write a real fitness goal — and a plan to reach it. SMART goals beat vague goals every time.

1
Paragraph 1
My Fitness Goal

Answer:

  • What is one fitness goal you want to improve in PE or at home?
  • Why did you choose this goal?
  • How will this goal help your body stay healthy or perform better?

Make sure your goal is SMART: Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, Time-bound.

Sentence Starters (optional):

  • "My fitness goal is…"
  • "I chose this goal because…"
  • "This goal will help me by…"
2
Paragraph 2
My Personal Fitness Plan

Answer:

  • What activity will you practice to reach your goal?
  • How often will you practice?
  • Who can help or encourage you?
  • How will you practice safely?

Sentence Starters (optional):

  • "My fitness plan is…"
  • "I will practice by…"
  • "I will stay safe by…"
📝Weekly Reflection

How will you know if your plan is working? What specific evidence will you track — number of reps, time, distance, how you feel? What will you change if you're NOT improving after 2 weeks?

assignments.title: My Fitness Goal Art Project
assignments.html:
Optima
Academy Online
Mission: Move!
5th Grade PE · Unit 1.16 · Goal Setting & Personal Fitness Plans
Unit 1.16

Show your fitness goal AND plan through art or media. A picture (or video, or comic) can communicate what words sometimes can't.

1
Goal
Use Art to Show Your Plan

You'll use art or media to show your fitness goal and how you plan to reach it.

2
Step 1
Choose ONE Way to Create
  • Draw a poster or picture
  • Create a digital drawing or slideshow
  • Make a short video or animation
  • Design a comic strip
  • Create a VR scene or model (if available)
3
Step 2
Your Project Must Include
  1. Your Fitness Goal — what do you want to get better at?
  2. Your Fitness Plan — what activity, how often will you practice?
  3. Benefits — how will this goal help your body stay healthy AND perform?
  4. Safety Tip — one way you'll stay safe while practicing
4
Helpful Prompts
  • "My fitness goal is…"
  • "I will practice by…"
  • "This goal helps my body by…"
  • "I will stay safe by…"
📝Weekly Reflection

Why did you choose art over writing for this project? What can a picture or video show about your goal that words alone can't? How do you know your art communicates the plan clearly — would a stranger understand it?

quizzes.title: Quiz 4: Movement & Ball Skills

questions.text: What is the difference between a HOP and a LEAP?

answers.text: A hop uses two feet to land; a leap uses one.
A hop pushes off and lands on the SAME foot; a leap pushes off one foot and lands on the OTHER.
A hop is sideways; a leap is forward.
A hop is silent; a leap is loud.

questions.text: When a baseball pitcher throws as hard as they can, where does MOST of their power come from?

answers.text: Just their throwing arm.
Their throwing wrist and fingers only.
The full kinetic chain — feet, hips, core, and shoulder all working together.
The catcher who tells them when to throw.

questions.text: Dante is kicking a soccer ball, but his shots keep flying weakly to the right. He plants his right foot 12 inches BEHIND the ball and tries to kick with his left foot. What's the most likely fix?

answers.text: Switch to a heavier ball — his kicks would suddenly be stronger.
Plant his right foot BESIDE the ball (about 6 inches to the side), so his hips can rotate through the kick.
Wear different shoes — that's the only thing that affects soccer kicks.
Kick with both feet at the same time.

questions.text: Humans are the only animals that can throw an object with both speed AND accuracy — our shoulder joint evolved a unique shape that allows this.

answers.text: True
False

questions.text: What is the name for the chain reaction where energy moves from your feet through your hips, core, and shoulder, out through your fingertips? (Two words.)

answers.text: kinetic chain
the kinetic chain

quizzes.description: Five questions covering Modules 1.7–1.9. Test your understanding of locomotor skills, the kinetic chain, throwing, catching, kicking, and striking.

quizzes.title: Quiz 5: Teamwork, Safety, Fitness Components & Goals

questions.text: Sara plays soccer for 30 minutes, three times a week. She also does push-ups every morning. Which TWO fitness components is she training the MOST?

answers.text: Flexibility and body composition.
Cardiovascular endurance and muscular strength.
Balance and coordination only.
Speed and reaction time only.

questions.text: Which of these is the BEST example of a SMART fitness goal?

answers.text: I want to get in shape someday.
I want to be the fastest runner in the school by the end of next week.
I will run a mile in under 9 minutes by April 30, by jogging for 20 minutes three times a week.
I want to never feel tired again.

questions.text: When you balance on one foot, your body uses THREE sources of information to stay steady. Which is NOT one of them?

answers.text: Your eyes (vision).
Your inner ear (which detects head motion).
Sensors in your joints and muscles (proprioception).
Your sense of smell.

questions.text: A team where every member feels safe speaking up and admitting mistakes is more likely to succeed than a team that just listens to its loudest player. This is called 'psychological safety.'

answers.text: True
False

questions.text: What is the term for moving your body to a steady beat or pattern? (Two words: an adjective ending in '-ic' and the word 'movement'.)

answers.text: rhythmic movement

quizzes.description: Final five questions covering Modules 1.10–1.16. Tests teamwork, sportsmanship, the 5 fitness components, balance, safety, and SMART goal setting.
